chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Isma'il ibn Abd al-Khaliq who said:

I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) while he was saying: 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar divorced his wife three times, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) counted it as one single divorce, and returned it to the Book and the Sunnah.'

key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ص: the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: How is triple divorce pronounced simultaneously counted in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar highlights the Shia juristic position that three simultaneous divorces constitute a single revocable divorce (talaq raj'i), contrasting with the Sunni view of them being irrevocable. It references the precedent of Abdullah ibn 'Umar, where the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) treated the triple pronouncement as one, thereby preserving the wife's right of return during the waiting period (iddah) without requiring a new marriage contract. This ruling underscores the principle of returning to the Quranic text and Prophetic Sunnah to mitigate hardship in marital dissolution.
